solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What bachelor did to restrain Irish eccentric

indicators.note: to restrain is to hold something in, so the bachelor's deed wraps round the Irish abbreviation

parts.note: a bachelor married nobody: WED plus O, the round letter for nothing

explanation.surface: A single man somehow keeps an odd Irishman under control.
explanation.walkthrough: A bachelor, by definition, wed O: married nobody, with O as zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an eccentric is an odd, unconventional person, a crank.

clue.text: Cold milk held up? It's addictive to a feline

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means lifted so the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a pinta is British slang for a pint of milk

explanation.surface: A cold carton of milk is delayed, and the cat craves something.
explanation.walkthrough: PINTA, British slang for a pint of milk, is read upwards because 'held up' in a down clue raises it.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: this herb of the mint family famously excites and intoxicates cats.

clue.text: Factor superhero represented as a normal occurrence

indicators.note: something represented is presented anew, so these letters are recast into a new order

explanation.surface: Some factor of a comic-book hero is portrayed as an everyday thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented as' rearranges FACTOR SUPERHERO.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom from golf, where par is the expected score: something typical and to be expected.

clue.text: Hide in part of Mediterranean island furthest from European heartland?

parts.note: the south-east corner, SE, of the island is the part furthest from central Europe
Crete is the large Greek island in the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: A question about hiding away in the remotest corner of a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' links: the south-eastern (SE) part of CRETE lies furthest from Europe's middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to conceal or stash something away, as in secreting a note in a pocket.

clue.text: Cosmetic party activity? Tories plug site devised to cover Conservative

indicators.note: to cover something is to go around it, so the shuffled letters enclose the abbreviation
something devised is contrived or worked out afresh, so these letters are arranged anew

explanation.surface: Tories promote a website made to protect one of their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devised' scrambles the three words before it; 'to cover' wraps that mix round the Conservative abbreviation. The question mark flags a playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: political action done for show, to look good, rather than to achieve anything real.

clue.text: Wise, possibly, counter argument seen around print and TV

indicators.note: the counter argument sits around the press term, enclosing it

parts.note: a con is an argument against, as in pros and cons
the media are newspapers and broadcasting together

explanation.surface: A shrewd rebuttal appears in newspapers and on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wise' is not shrewd but Ernie Wise, of the British comic double act Morecambe and Wise; 'possibly' marks him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Ernie Wise was a famous British funny man, half of a much-loved TV double act.

clue.text: Salesman getting a lot of ridicule, day before suspension

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: a lot of a word is most of it, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: to rib is to tease or ridicule
an eve is the day before an event

explanation.surface: A salesman, mocked at length, gets off the day before a ban begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' trims RIB to RI.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a stay or postponement, especially of a punishment, is a suspension of it.

clue.text: Distinct group almost infiltrated by a painter

indicators.note: being infiltrated means having something get inside, so the shortened group takes in the pieces
almost means the last letter is left off the word

parts.note: a septet is a group of seven
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword painter

explanation.surface: A particular set nearly gets penetrated by an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the seven-piece group by its last letter; 'infiltrated by' slips A plus the Academician inside it, leaving the final TE outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: separate things are distinct, apart from one another.

clue.text: Missile made by revolutionary firm in Texas and Spain

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the whole assembly is read backwards
the firm sits in the state's abbreviation

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A weapon produced by a radical company based in Texas and Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives TE(CO)X, plus E makes TECOXE, which 'revolutionary' turns into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a French-made anti-ship missile, famous from the Falklands War.

clue.text: Island club overlooking hotel

indicators.note: to overlook is to miss out, so the letter is ignored

parts.note: a cosh is a heavy club or bludgeon
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A golf club sits above a seaside hotel on some island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooking' suggests a view but means leaving H out of COSH.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: one of the Greek Dodecanese islands, also the home of the lettuce.

clue.text: Change in coaches one's put out with official backing

indicators.note: put out means removed, so the numeral is taken away

parts.note: railway coaches make up trains
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so this word is read in reverse

parts.note: a ref is a referee, a match official

explanation.surface: A switch of coaches, with someone ejected, approved by an official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coaches' means railway carriages, not buses or trainers; 'put out' removes the I, and 'backing' turns the official round.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to move between trains or buses, or to shift something elsewhere.

clue.text: What's recalled in politician giving explanation

indicators.note: the questioning word goes in the politician

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative politician

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: eh? is a way of saying what?

explanation.surface: A politician gives an account of what he remembers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns EH into HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a hypothesis or account offered to explain facts.

clue.text: Repair decorator discharged for acquisitive type

indicators.note: discharged suggests let go in disorder, so these letters are scattered and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A painter is sacked from a mending job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discharged' rearranges REPAIR DECORATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a financier who buys up stakes to take over other companies, greedy for acquisitions.

clue.text: Disorder curtailed in port

indicators.note: curtailed means having its tail cut, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a riot is public disorder

explanation.surface: Unrest is cut short in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' drops the last letter of RIOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian harbour city.

clue.text: Line in badly finished work by yard showing irregular discolouring?

indicators.note: the line letter goes in the shoddy work

parts.note: a botch is a bungled job

explanation.surface: A shoddy paint job next to a yard leaves patchy stains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places Y next to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: blotchy skin or paint is marked with uneven patches of colour.

clue.text: Artist becoming fat and round having been around long time

indicators.note: the fat has been put around the period of time, enclosing it

parts.note: lard is pig fat
an eon is an age, a very long time
O is a round letter

explanation.surface: A painter grows plump and portly after many years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having been around' puts the fat round the age; 'becoming' and 'and' only link the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Leonardo da Vinci, the Renaissance painter of the Mona Lisa.

clue.text: Journalists on Telegraph rival getting appointment for TV programme?

indicators.note: on here means attached to, so the journalists come after the newspaper they work for

parts.note: The Times is a rival British daily to the Telegraph
a lot is a group of people, here the staff writers, as in 'that lot'

explanation.surface: Reporters from a competing paper land a broadcast booking.
explanation.walkthrough: Split five and three, the answer describes the staff of a rival national newspaper to the Telegraph.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the scheduled period when a broadcast is shown is its allotted place in the schedule.

clue.text: Plausible talk about a Northern toady

indicators.note: the patter goes about, surrounding, the other pieces

parts.note: a spiel is glib, persuasive patter

explanation.surface: Smooth chatter about a northerner who sucks up to people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SPIEL round A N.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: a fawning, servile follower, like a devoted dog.

clue.text: Bother type having switch of direction

indicators.note: left becomes right, so the L letter is swapped for R

parts.note: ilk means type or kind

explanation.surface: A kind of thing that changes course.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the L (left) of ILK for R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to annoy or irritate someone.

clue.text: Obstreperous agent consuming drink after promotion

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so the agent holds the drink inside

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

indicators.note: promoted means raised, so in a down clue this word reads upwards

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A rowdy spy drinks heavily after being promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after promotion' sends the drink upwards in this down light; 'consuming' tucks the turned wine inside the agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: bad-tempered and awkward, unruly; British informal for truculent.

clue.text: Plain lot to touch a monk unexpectedly

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests things turning out otherwise, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Plenty of people suddenly reach out to a monk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' means unattractive here, not simple or flat ground; 'unexpectedly' rearranges LOT TO TOUCH A MONK.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an unattractive, homely person is plain in appearance.

clue.text: Unique act implied by a player getting red card?

definitions.meaning: a single event that will not be repeated
a red card sends a footballer off the pitch, leaving a team one man short

explanation.surface: A singular event is suggested by a footballer being sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'implied by' links the two senses; split as ONE OFF it describes the sending-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something done once only, a unique occurrence.

clue.text: Speak first to soprano in upcoming musical work, ignoring volunteers

indicators.note: the soprano letter goes in the reworked composition
ignoring means leaving out, so these letters are dropped
in a down clue, upcoming means rising, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: a toccata is a virtuoso keyboard piece
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A singer is approached within a rising piece of music, minus the reservists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upcoming' turns the keyboard piece upwards to ATACCOT; 'ignoring' removes the volunteers to leave ACCOT; 'in' places the soprano inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to approach and address someone, often boldly.

clue.text: Islands capital captured in main assault

indicators.note: captured in means held inside, so the letters sit within these words

explanation.surface: A city is taken in a large-scale attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captured in' finds it spanning mAIN ASSAUlt.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the capital city of the Bahamas, an island nation.

clue.text: Fantastic church defending a work of a charity

parts.note: outré means bizarre or fantastic

explanation.surface: A wonderful church protects the good deeds of a charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defending' just links, setting CH beside A.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: community work that extends services out to people in need.

clue.text: Rent in Yorkshire place that's not feasible

indicators.note: not removes the following idea, so those letters go

parts.note: Ripon is a cathedral city in North Yorkshire
on means feasible, as in 'that's not on'

explanation.surface: Renting in a Yorkshire town is not workable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' is a tear, not a payment; RIPON is a cathedral city in Yorkshire, and 'not' takes away ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a rent is a split or tear in fabric.

clue.text: Offensive characteristic of harmony Spice Girl dropped

indicators.note: dropped means let go, so these letters leave the word

parts.note: melodious means tuneful, a quality of harmony
Mel B and Mel C were Spice Girls

explanation.surface: Something rude about the harmonies after a pop singer quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' removes MEL from MELODIOUS; the Spice Girls were a 1990s British pop group with two Mels.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: hateful, repugnant, highly offensive.

clue.text: Revolutionary individual originally associated with top duke, one avoiding struggle

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: a cap is a top or lid

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: dukes is slang for fists, from rhyming slang

explanation.surface: A rebel, linked to a leading aristocrat, ducks out of a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' turns CAP round; 'duke' is slang for a fist, from Cockney rhyming slang Duke of Yorks = forks = fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: someone opposed to war and violence refuses to fight.
